genesis.40.p1.b1.text: … and imprisoned them in the house of the captain of the guard, the same prison where Joseph was confined. The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he became their personal attendant.

genesis.40.p1.b2.text: Some time later, the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master, the king of Egypt. Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,

genesis.40.p1.b3.text: After they had been in custody for some time …

genesis.40.p2.b1.text: both of these men—the Egyptian king’s cupbearer and baker, who were being held in the prison—had a dream on the same night, and each dream had its own meaning.

genesis.40.p2.b2.text: Why are your faces so downcast today?

genesis.40.p2.b3.text: We both had dreams … but there is no one to interpret them.

genesis.40.p2.b4.text: Don’t interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.

genesis.40.p3.b1.text: In my dream there was a vine before me,

genesis.40.p3.b2.text: and on the vine were three branches. As it budded, its blossoms opened and its clusters ripened into grapes.

genesis.40.p3.b3.text: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into his cup, and placed the cup in his hand.”

genesis.40.p4.b1.text: This is the interpretation: The three branches are three days.

genesis.40.p4.b2.text: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore your position. You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand …

genesis.40.p4.b3.text: But when it goes well for you, please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh, that he might bring me out of this prison.

genesis.40.p4.b4.text: For I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing for which they should have put me in this dungeon.”

genesis.40.p5.b1.text: I too had a dream: There were three baskets of white bread on my head.

genesis.40.p5.b2.text: In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”

genesis.40.p5.b3.text: This is the interpretation: The three baskets are three days.

genesis.40.p5.b4.text: Within three days Pharaoh will … hang you on a tree …

genesis.40.p6.b1.text: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he held a feast for all his officials,

genesis.40.p6.b2.text: … in their presence he lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

genesis.40.p6.b3.text: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position, so that he once again placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.

genesis.40.p6.b4.text: But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had described to them in his interpretation.

genesis.40.p7.b1.text: The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.
